<reflection>
The fitting results from the first experiment show that all 20 candidate mechanisms have very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, with differences less than 0.44. This indicates that the initial condition (S=1.0, cat=0.01, P=0.0) does not provide sufficient discriminative power to rule out any mechanism. My aim for the first turn was to obtain baseline kinetic data, which was achieved, but now I need to design a new experiment that can reduce uncertainty across the entire set of plausible mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I hypothesize that increasing the catalyst concentration will reveal nonlinear dependencies in the reaction rate that are characteristic of mechanisms involving catalyst dimerization (e.g., M2, M3, M19), catalyst activation (e.g., M6, M8), or concentration-dependent deactivation (e.g., M9, M13, M18, M20). By setting catalyst to 0.05 M while keeping substrate at 1.0 M and product at 0.0, I create a condition where the rate should scale linearly with catalyst for simple mechanisms (M1) but may show deviations for others. This experiment will probe the functional form of catalyst dependence without pushing into saturation or depletion regimes, making it informative for a wide range of mechanisms simultaneously.
</hypothesis>
